business_problem: Terray Therapeutics needed to search an almost infinite chemical space with generative models, but multi-node training, terabyte-scale datasets, and iterative hyperparameter experiments were too cumbersome on a mix of on-premises and generic cloud systems.
solution_summary: Terray built the COATI and TerraBind model-development workflow on NVIDIA DGX Cloud, NVIDIA Base Command Platform, and later NVIDIA cuEquivariance. The company starts from a massive experimental engine that measures hundreds of millions of molecule-target interactions daily and stores more than 50 billion biophysical measurements. Those data are used to train COATI, a multimodal encoder-decoder that translates molecules into numerical representations and back again so the company can generate new compounds with desired properties. DGX Cloud simplified multi-node training and Base Command Platform standardized job launch and orchestration, which let Terray move from manual remote-cluster management to push-button 32-GPU experiments. Terray then accelerated TerraBind models further with cuEquivariance, improving potency-prediction performance while cutting the time and cost required to iterate on new drug candidates.

solution_components.role: Schedules and orchestrates Terray's cloud training jobs and dataset workflows.

solution_components.name: COATI

solution_components.name: NVIDIA cuEquivariance
solution_components.role: Accelerates TerraBind kernels for faster potency-prediction training and inference.

data_flow: Terray's experimental measurements feed COATI training on DGX Cloud, Base Command orchestrates large distributed runs, generated molecule embeddings flow into screening and optimization loops, and cuEquivariance-accelerated TerraBind models return potency and structure predictions for new candidates.
business_outcome: Terray increased resource utilization by 4x compared with alternative clouds, cut model training from a week to a day, and later used cuEquivariance to accelerate TerraBind by 3x to 4x with about 70% cost savings, giving researchers far more room to search for rare high-value molecules.
